## IMC data 

### Tumor panel 

#### Preprocessing 

```{r}
tumor_key <- read_csv("/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/tumor_panel/data_analysis/BlockForest/tumor_key_features.csv")

# Preprocessing as suggested by Boeva (Cell Reports Methods)
# Step 1: Only keep columns with less than 10% of NA values 
## This often removes INT values
remove <- colnames(tumor_key)[colMeans(is.na(tumor_key)) > 0.1]
remove <- remove[!remove %in% c("status_OS", "OS_months")]

tumor_selected <- tumor_key %>% select(-remove)

# Step 2: Missing numerical values can be imputed (Median across non-missing samples OR minimum for INT values)
summary(is.na(tumor_selected))

tumor_selected[] <- lapply(colnames(tumor_selected), function(colname) {
  if (colname %in% c("status_OS", "OS_months")) {
    return(tumor_selected[[colname]])  
  } else {
    # If column has NA and is not excluded, replace NA with column minimum
    col <- tumor_selected[[colname]]
    if (any(is.na(col)) & str_detect(colname, "INT")) {
      col[is.na(col)] <- min(col, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
    return(col)
  }
})

summary(is.na(tumor_selected))

# Step 3: To implement - Correlation removal? >95% correlation

# Add specific prefix
colnames(tumor_selected)[4:ncol(tumor_selected)] <- paste0("IMC_TU_",colnames(tumor_selected)[4:ncol(tumor_selected)])
tumor_selected <- as.data.frame(tumor_selected)
```

# 2. BlockForest survival prediction

```{r}
library(blockForest)
```

## Load and select data

```{r}
metadata_selected <- read_csv("/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/tumor_panel/data_analysis/BlockForest/key_features_processed.csv")
```

```{r}
# Select colnames based on prefix
selected <- colnames(metadata_selected)#[str_detect(colnames(metadata_selected),"IMC")]

# Select either pT/ISUP_simple or pT/ISUP_combined
selected <- selected[!str_detect(selected, "combined")] #selects simple

meta <- metadata_selected %>% select(PID, status_OS, OS_months, all_of(selected)) %>% filter(complete.cases(.))
```

```{r}
# Make sure stage, grade and necrose are encoded as characters
meta$CLIN_pT_simple <- as.character(meta$CLIN_pT_simple)
meta$CLIN_ISUP_simple <- as.character(meta$CLIN_ISUP_simple)
meta$CLIN_necrose <- as.character(meta$CLIN_necrose)
```

## Encoding 

```{r}
# Perform preprocessing
meta[] <- lapply(names(meta), function(col_name) {
  if (col_name %in% c("PID", "status_OS", "OS_months")) {
    return(meta[[col_name]])  # Return the column as is
  } else {
    if (is.numeric(meta[[col_name]])) {
      return(as.vector(scale(meta[[col_name]]))) # Scale numerical columns (Z-score)
    } 
    else if (is.character(meta[[col_name]])) {
      return(as.factor(meta[[col_name]])) # Convert character columns to factors
    } else {
      return(meta[[col_name]])
    }
  }
})

str(meta)
```

## Correlation reduction

### Numeric

```{r, fig.width=16, fig.height=16}
# 1. Check statistical association of numerical variables
cor_test <- meta %>% select(where(is.numeric), -status_OS,-OS_months)

cor_matrix <- cor(cor_test,method = "pearson")

corrplot(cor_matrix, method="shade", col=brewer.pal(n=8, name="RdBu"),  
         type="upper", order="hclust",hclust.method = "ward.D2", 
         addCoef.col = "black", addCoefasPercent = F,
         tl.col="black", tl.srt=40, 
         diag=FALSE
)

# Identify pairs with cor > 0.95
high_corr_pairs <- which(abs(cor_matrix) > 0.95 & lower.tri(cor_matrix), arr.ind = TRUE)
high_corr_pairs_df <- data.frame(
  Var1 = rownames(cor_matrix)[high_corr_pairs[, 1]],
  Var2 = colnames(cor_matrix)[high_corr_pairs[, 2]],
  Correlation = cor_matrix[high_corr_pairs]
)
```

```{r}
# Remove specific pairs 
removed_numeric <- c("IMC_TU_D_ICAM1_dom", "IMC_TU_D_mTORhi_dom", "IMC_TU_INT_CD8_T_cell__TU_HLADRhi")

meta_fil <- meta %>% select(-all_of(removed_numeric))
```

### Categorical 

```{r}
# 2. Check statistical association of categorical variables
chi_test <- colnames(meta %>% select(where(is.factor), -status_OS,-OS_months))

out_p <- list()

for(i in chi_test){
  for(y in chi_test){
    if(i != y){
    out <- meta %>% select(PID, any_of(i), any_of(y)) %>% unique %>% select(-PID) %>% group_by(all_of(i)) %>% table() %>%
      as.data.frame
    cur_test <- out %>% pivot_wider(names_from = i, id_cols = y, values_from = Freq) %>% column_to_rownames(y)
    cur_test_out <- chisq.test(cur_test)
    out_p[paste0(i,"_",y)] <- cur_test_out$p.value
    }
  }
}

# FDR-correct p-values
p_values <- unlist(out_p)
adjusted_p_values <- p.adjust(p_values, method = "BH")
out_p_adjust <- as.list(adjusted_p_values)

# Extract direct comparison p-values
direct_comp <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(chi_test), ncol = length(chi_test), dimnames = list(chi_test, chi_test))

for (i in chi_test) {
  for (j in chi_test) {
    if (i == j) {
      direct_comp[i, j] <- 1
    } else {
      comp_name <- paste(i, j, sep = "_")
      rev_comp_name <- paste(j, i, sep = "_")
      if (comp_name %in% names(out_p_adjust)) {
        direct_comp[i, j] <- out_p_adjust[[comp_name]]
      } else if (rev_comp_name %in% names(out_p_adjust)) {
        direct_comp[i, j] <- out_p_adjust[[rev_comp_name]]
      }
    }
  }
}

# Print the square matrix
corrplot(-log10(direct_comp), 
         is.corr = FALSE, 
         diag = FALSE, 
         tl.col = "black",
         type="upper", 
         col = COL1("Blues",100),
         method = "shade",
         bg = "lightgrey", addCoef.col = "black")


# Identify pairs with 
high_corr_pairs <- which(abs(direct_comp) < 0.01 & lower.tri(direct_comp), arr.ind = TRUE)

high_corr_pairs_df <- data.frame(
  Var1 = rownames(direct_comp)[high_corr_pairs[, 1]],
  Var2 = colnames(direct_comp)[high_corr_pairs[, 2]],
  Correlation = direct_comp[high_corr_pairs]
)
```

## Folds

```{r}
library(caret)
folds <- createDataPartition(y$status_OS, p = 0.75, times = 5)
```

## Define blocks 

```{r}
# Create blocks 
# Initialize empty list for blocks
block <- list()

# Define blocks based on column names containing "CLIN" and "IMC"
```

## Perform BlockForest

### 5fold CV (Outer)

#### Define function 

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(blockForest)
library(survival)

# Create a function for 5 fold outer cross-validation
cross_validate_blockforest <- function(x, y, folds, block) {
  results <- vector("list", length(folds))
  
  for (i in seq_along(folds)) {
    
    print(paste("CV iteration:", i))
    
    # Split the data into training and test sets
    x_train <- x[folds[[i]],]
    x_test <- x[-folds[[i]],]

    y_train <- y[folds[[i]],]
    y_test <- y[-folds[[i]],]
    
    # Train the blockForest model
    blockforobj <- blockfor(X = x_train, 
                            y = as.matrix(y_train), 
                            blocks = block,
                            splitrule = "extratrees", 
                            block.method = "BlockForest",
                            num.trees = 2000,
                            nsets = 300, 
                            num.trees.pre = 1500,
                            always.select.block = 1,
                            num.threads = 30,
                            importance = "permutation")
    
    # Make predictions on the test data
    predres <- predict(blockforobj$forest, data = x_test)
    
    # Store the results for evaluation, e.g., store predicted survival functions
    results[[i]] <- list(predictions = predres,
                         actual_test = x_test,
                         actual_surv = y_test, 
                         variable_importance = blockforobj$forest$variable.importance)
    
    gc()
  }
  
  return(results)
}
```

## Run and save results

```{r}
# Run cross-validation
set.seed(22)
cv_results <- cross_validate_blockforest(x, y, folds, block)

# Adjust naming!
saveRDS(cv_results, "/mnt/central_nas/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/tumor_panel/data_analysis/BlockForest/BF_IMConly_tumor_panel_zscored.rds")
```

### Integrated Brier Score

```{r, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=4.5}
# Initialize list to store IBS scores for each cross-validation result
ibs_scores_list <- list()

# Loop over each cross-validation result object using lapply
ibs_scores_list <- lapply(cv_results_list, function(res_obj) {
  # Apply function over each element in the result object (each fold in cross-validation)
  sapply(res_obj, function(res) {
    # Check if row counts match between actual_surv and actual_test
    if (nrow(res$actual_surv) != nrow(res$actual_test)) {
      stop("Row count mismatch between actual_surv and actual_test")
    }
    
    # Define test data
    test_data <- cbind(res$actual_surv, res$actual_test)
    
    # Time points in test data
    times_test <- sort(unique(test_data$OS_months))
    if(!0 %in% times_test){
    times_test <- c(0, times_test) # Add timepoint 0 as baseline (if not included)
    }
    
    # Time points in prediction
    times_pred <- res$predictions$unique.death.times
    
    # Find the nearest indices for each desired time in the unique death times
    time_indices <- sapply(times_test, function(t) which.min(abs(times_pred - t)))
    
    # Extract predicted survival probabilities at the specified times
    aligned_surv_probs <- res$predictions$survival[, time_indices, drop = FALSE]
    
    # Calculate prediction error curve (PEC)
    pec_obj <- pec(
      object = list("BlockForest" = aligned_surv_probs),
      formula = Surv(OS_months, status_OS) ~ 1,
      cens.model = "marginal",
      exact = TRUE,
      data = test_data
    )
    
    # Define the time range of interest for IBS
    #IBSrange <- quantile(test_data$OS_months, 0.9)
    IBSrange <- max(test_data$OS_months)
    
    # Calculate the CRPS and extract the IBS score
    crps_val <- crps(pec_obj, start = 0, times = IBSrange)
    ibs_score <- crps_val[2] # Adjust if necessary based on your specific data structure
    
    return(ibs_score)
  })
})

# Convert scores to dataframe
out_ibs <- data.frame(fold = 1:5, t(do.call("rbind", ibs_scores_list))) %>% pivot_longer(2:ncol(.), names_to = "model", values_to = "IBS")

# Plot
library(ggpubr)
ggplot(out_ibs, aes(x = reorder(model,-IBS), y = IBS, fill = model))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  #coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.5,1))+
  theme_classic()+
  stat_compare_means(ref.group = "CLIN_only", paired = FALSE, method = "t.test", method.args = list(alternative = "less", label = "p.format"))+
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "RdBu")+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))+
  xlab("Models")+
  ylab("Integrated Brier Score")
```



### Concordance (Uno)


```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
# Initialize list to store concordance scores for each cross-validation result
concordance_scores_list <- list()

# Loop over each cross-validation result object using lapply
concordance_scores_list <- lapply(cv_results_list, function(res_obj) {
  # Apply function over each element in the result object (each fold in cross-validation)
  sapply(res_obj, function(res) {
    out <- concordance(Surv(res$actual_surv[, 1], res$actual_surv[, 2]) ~ rowSums(res$predictions$survival), timewt = "n/G2")
    return(out$concordance)
  })
})

out_concordance <- data.frame(fold = 1:5, t(do.call("rbind", concordance_scores_list))) %>% pivot_longer(2:ncol(.), names_to = "model", values_to = "concordance")

library(ggpubr)
ggplot(out_concordance, aes(x = reorder(model,-concordance), y = concordance, fill = model))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  #coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.5,1))+
  theme_classic()+
  stat_compare_means(ref.group = "CLIN_only", paired = FALSE, method = "t.test", method.args = list(alternative = "greater", label = "p.format"))+
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "RdBu")+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))+
  xlab("Models")+
  ylab("Concordance (Uno)")
```

### Check specific model 

#### Kaplan-Meier and risk group definition

```{r}
dataset <- cv_results_1
surv_plots <- list()
data_out <- list()

for(i in seq_along(dataset)){
  res <- dataset[[i]]
  out <- cbind(res$actual_surv,chf = rowSums(res$predictions$chf))
  out_df <- out %>% mutate(risk_group = ifelse(chf > median(chf), "high", "low"), fold = i) %>% rownames_to_column("PID")

  #Plot specific survival curves
  fit <- survfit(Surv(out_df$OS_months, out_df$status_OS) ~ risk_group, data = out_df)

  surv_plots[[i]] <- fit
  data_out[[i]] <- out_df
}

# Plot all curves for each CV fold
library(survival)
library(survminer)
ggsurvplot_list(surv_plots, 
                data = data_out,
                risk.table = TRUE, # Add risk table
                risk.table.col = "strata", # Change risk table color by groups
                linetype = "strata", # Change line type by groups
                surv.median.line = "hv", # Specify median survival
                ggtheme = theme_classic(), # Change ggplot2 theme
                palette = "Set1",
                conf.int = TRUE
                )

## Pick a specific fold
ggsurvplot(surv_plots[[2]], 
          pval = TRUE,
          risk.table = TRUE, # Add risk table
          risk.table.col = "strata", # Change risk table color by groups
          linetype = "strata", # Change line type by groups
          surv.median.line = "hv", # Specify median survival
          ggtheme = theme_classic(), # Change ggplot2 theme
          palette = "Set1",
          conf.int = TRUE
)

# Display averaged chf across all folds
data_comb <- do.call("rbind", data_out)

data_comb <- data_comb %>% group_by(PID) %>% mutate(mean_chf = mean(chf)) %>% select(PID, OS_months, status_OS, mean_chf) %>% unique() %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(risk_group = ifelse(mean_chf > median(mean_chf), "high", "low"))

fit <- survfit(Surv(data_comb$OS_months, data_comb$status_OS) ~ risk_group, data = data_comb)

ggsurvplot(fit, 
          pval = TRUE,

          surv.median.line = "hv", # Specify median survival
          ggtheme = theme_classic(), # Change ggplot2 theme
          palette = "Set1",
          conf.int = TRUE
)
```
